Coram : Vinay Joshi & Valmiki Sa Menezes, Jj.

This petition under Article 226 of the Constitution read with section 482 of the Code of Criminal
Procedure, is seeking to quash the Fir relating to Crime No.365/2023 registered with Police Station
Wadi, District Nagpur City for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B r/w
34 of the Indian Penal Code.
3. The contention of applicants is that the registration of Fir itself is a misuse of the process of law.
According to the applicants, the dispute was purely of civil in nature.
However, after remaining unsuccessful in civil litigation the informant has approached to the Magistrate seeking directions to register the FIR.

It is submitted that the informant has suppressed about the wp 422.23. 2/5 4 pendency of civil suit as well as adverse interim order passed against him by the learned Magistrate,
while obtaining directions to the Police to register the crime.
According to the applicants, this is completely a misuse of the process of law initiated with ulterior motive to settle the score.
4. The informant has alleged that the applicants in connivance with co-accused has prepared false documents relating to subject land in which the informant and her mother had undivided share.
Precisely, the grievance was in respect of peace of land admeasuring 2.46 H out of Kh. No.55.2.
It appears that the informant's mother is claiming share through her mother in the subject property.

In that regard the informant stated that despite informant's mother being sharer the property has changed the hands by suppressing the factual position and thus it is a case of fabrication of false Hasmukh S/O. Hirjibhai Rathod And ... vs State Of Mah. Thr. Pso, Ps Wadi, Dist. ... on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33595464/
1 documents in the nature of sale and further alienations.

The learned Counsel for the applicants took us through Regular Civil Suit No.186/2021 filed on 02-01-2021 by the mother of informant seeking declaration that a sale deed dated 31- 10-2008 executed by some of the co-accused in favour of applicants pertaining to the same land be declared as null and void and not binding on their sharer.
Moreover, in wp 422.23. 3/5 4 the same suit, the informant's mother is seeking declaration about her 1/9th undivided share.
In the said suit, the informant's mother has also applied for grant of temporary injunction.

However, the learned Civil Judge considered the case on set parameters held that the informant's mother/plaintiff failed to establish prima facie case which resulted into rejection of temporary injunction application vide order dated 25-07-2022.
It reveals from the copy of the plaint and impugned order that the informant's mother Alka was claiming property rights through her mother Anandibai.

Trial Court gave prima face consideration to the rival submissions and ultimately held that there is no material that the informant's mother Alka was daughter of Anandibai and thus it weighed to the trial Court in rejecting the interim relief.

In the wake of such position, the informant's mother Alka being failed in securing interim relief, through her son i.e.
informant Advocate Ashish has applied to the Magistrate seeking directions against the Police to register a crime by invoking the provisions of Section 156(3) of the Cr.P.C.
5.

Same grievance was agitated in the Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. application pertaining to undivided share of informant's mother Alka while claiming that the sale transaction was fraudulent and thus there is a wp 422.23. 4/5 4 cheating, fabrication and fraud.
Particularly emphasis is led that the said application is totally silent regarding pendency of suit as well as refusal of temporary relief by competent Civil Court.

6. Moreover, it is argued that the sale deed under which the applicants are claiming right is of the year 2018 and now after lapse of 15 years, the criminal case has been filed.
7.
Moreover, it is submitted that the informant did not follow the per-requisite compliance in terms of Section 154(3) of the Cr.P.C. before approaching to the Magistrate.

Prima facie, it is evident that on failure in securing interim order in civil suit, the informant for the same cause has approached to the Magistrate and thus there appears to be considerable force in the contention that a civil dispute has been coloured as a criminal prosecution to achieve the ultimate desire.

Having peculiar facts of this case, it is necessary to decide the petition expeditiously as the Police machinery would be unnecessarily required to investigate into the matter if prosecution is required to be untenable.

Thus, being exceptional case, we deem it appropriate to stay the investigation.
8.
In view of above, issue notice for final wp 422.23. 5/5 4 disposal to the non-applicants, returnable after four weeks.
9. The investigation shall be stayed till the next date.
10. Learned APP waives notice for the State.
